description: Authored ground truth for the synthetic Meridia replay. The world is fictional; every event below actually happens in it on the stated date. 'gold' is the correct typed transition an ideal perception layer would file for that event; the oracle lane feeds these directly. 'articles' is how many corpus pieces the generator writes for the event (>1 = duplicate coverage of one causal event, which the pipeline must not double-fire). Distractor entries (gold.action == IGNORE) are real articles about the fictional region that match no indicator.

truth.note: The strait reopens 2026-09-12 (inside H3's tranche) and transit sustains >= 70% of baseline from 2026-09-24.

events.summary: Coalition naval forces report new sea mines laid across the southern Meridia channel; two bulk carriers turn back.
Regional fishing fleets dispute quota allocations in waters 200nm east of the strait; talks scheduled.
Direct talks between the blockading power and the riparian coalition resume in Qoros under neutral mediation.
Lloyd-equivalent tracking data shows daily transits at roughly 4 percent of the pre-crisis baseline; brokers describe traffic as a trickle.
A products tanker is seized by fast attack craft near the strait's western approach; crew detained.
Port authority east of the strait announces a five-year container terminal expansion plan unrelated to the blockade.
Marine insurers publish updated Meridia route pricing; the normalization index stands at 12 of 100, barely above crisis floor.
Two major insurance syndicates withdraw Meridia hull coverage entirely rather than re-price it; coverage availability is now a distinct question from price.

gold.missing_direction: Coverage WITHDRAWAL (availability) is not captured by the insurance_normalization price index; needs its own observable or indicator.

events.summary: Both sides announce a temporary maritime de-escalation understanding; no transit arrangements specified, no timetable, terms unpublished.

gold.reason: Material to the question but matches no pre-committed indicator: no named transit mechanism, no date, unverifiable terms.

events.summary: A five-nation escort framework named Operation Open Water is announced; first escorted convoy scheduled within two weeks.
Tracking data shows daily transits recovering to about 15 percent of baseline as escorted movements begin.
Indicator-cleanup session: red-team review of the recovery trend recorded; devil's advocate finds no strong counter-evidence (score 0.4).

gold.challenge: Could the escorted-convoy recovery stall if insurers balk? Reviewed: clearance contracts and insurance repricing argue no.

events.summary: The blockading power's energy ministry reports record domestic refinery output; analysts debate sanctions leakage.
Clearance consortium awarded contracts for mine disposal and wreck salvage across the southern channel; survey vessels deploy.
Joint decree announces the strait will formally reopen to commercial transit on 12 September under escort and insurance protocols.
First post-decree convoys transit in both directions; tracking shows daily transits near 38 percent of baseline.
Insurance normalization index rises to 64 as war-risk premiums fall for escorted transits.
A cruise operator announces it will resume regional itineraries next season, citing improving outlook; no transit data included.
Daily transits reach 78 percent of the pre-crisis baseline for the fifth consecutive day; brokers call the recovery sustained.
